item.title: Skubal’s Record Deal Could Break White Sox Free Agency
item.description: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images The Chicago White Sox have a narrow window to fix their pitching, but the market is shifting beneath their feet. Tarik Skubal is likely to shatter every record for a pitcher with a deal worth eight years and $355 million, according to ESPN . That number is the average of 27 projections from insiders polled by Kiley McDaniel. It is a massive sum that could drain the payroll for years to come. The 2026-27 free agent class is considered one of the weakest in a decade. They need help, but the top tier of the market is priced out of reach. The Skubal Health Question Skubal will be 30 in 2027 and posted a 2.72 ERA with 186 strikeouts this season. His stats are elite, yet his medical history raises red flags for a long-term commitment. He had Tommy John surgery in college and elbow surgery in 2022. He even underwent a procedure in May to remove loose bodies from his elbow. That minimally invasive surgery allowed him to pitch at a Cy Young level for the rest of the season. The White Sox cannot ignore this risk. The team paid a record price for an arm with three past surgeries. The Peralta Pivot Chasing Skubal might be a mistake when better value exists elsewhere. The White Sox need starting pitchers and position players more than anything else, says Yahoo Sports . While the market has more starting pitching talent than outfielders, the best position players like Randy Arozarena are still available. Pursuing Freddy Peralta makes more sense than betting the farm on Skubal. Yahoo Sports notes that going after Peralta or Michael King while also targeting top position players is a tall order. The team has six players entering free agency, including pitchers Erick Fedde and Sean Newcomb, per Sports Mockery . Newcomb threw 90.1 innings with a 3.09 ERA last season, per Sports Mockery. The Sox must find a way to fill holes without breaking the bank on one risky arm. The collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec 1. They have to weigh the cost of a $355 million contract against the need for immediate depth. If they overspend on Skubal, they might lose out on the position players they also need.

The Valkyries and the City of San Francisco will host the parade along the city's Embarcadero on Wednesday, Nov. 1. Here's what you need to know. What time will the parade start? Fans can begin lining up along the parade route at 9 a.m. on the bay Side of the Embarcadero. The parade will start at noon and expected to end at 2 p.m. Where will the parade be? The parade will start at noon at the Ferry Building, travel along the Embarcadero, and end at King and 2nd streets. Who will be there? The team, coaches, staff and city leaders will all be there to celebrate the historic win. According to the Golden State Valkyries, Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie, San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan, and city officials from across the Bay, are expected to be at the championship parade. Gabby Williams, who was named WNBA Finals Most Valuable Player, will bang the GSV drum alongside Mayor Daniel Lurie to start the parade, the team said. item.title: Arsenal win at Liverpool to go three points clear at league summit
item.description: Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha (L) and Arsenal's Kai Havertz battle for the ball during the English Premier League soccer match between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield. (is associated with: «Arsenal win at Liverpool to go three points clear at league summit») Peter Byrne/PA Wire/dpa Arsenal recorded a first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years but needed some help from Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker, whose first-half error led to Kai Havertz’s solitary goal in the 1-0 win. Not since manager Mikel Arteta was running the Gunners’ midfield in 2012 had they tasted victory in the red half of Merseyside and they were tested to the limit in ending end that run. However, if it is one thing Arteta’s side are well-drilled at it is seeing out games having maximized their opportunities and the celebrations in front of the visiting fans having moved top of the table showed how significant they felt this result was. And while most of the football was played by Liverpool after going behind it did not bring any rewards – partly due to poor judgement and execution but also bad luck. How Jurrien Timber’s tug on the shirt of Alexander Isak as he tried to connect with a header escaped the eagle eye of VAR will remain a question, especially as they were quick to look into a more regular coming together of Cody Gakpo and Christos Tzolis. By then the hosts were already behind after another miscalculation by Alisson. A week ago against Brighton the Brazil international had got away with a few loose passes in the win against Brighton. Arsenal were not so forgiving. His attempted pass to Jeremy Jacquet gave the centre-back no chance of retaining possession and the loose ball was seized upon by Arsenal, who moved it the right where Noni Madueke and Declan Rice combined for Havertz to tap in at the far post. The margins were always going to be tight in a match between the current champions, who have won all five league games when scoring the game’s first this season, and their predecessors and that one error proved to be the difference as for all their pressure Liverpool failed to test David Raya. Much of that was down to the hosts’ lack of composure in the final third – Raya did not have to make a save – and Arsenal’s experience at doing the necessary dirty work to deny those opportunities. item.title: Cologne's El Mala brothers grab draw at Union, Frankfurt beat Hamburg
item.description: Cologne's Malek El Mala (R) celebrates scoring his side's first goal with his brother Said El Mala during the German Bundesliga soccer match between 1. FC Union Berlin and 1. FC Cologne at An der Alten Foersterei. (is associated with: «Cologne's El Mala brothers grab draw at Union, Frankfurt beat Hamburg») Soeren Stache/dpa Cologne's Malek El Mala scored on his Bundesliga debut to outshine younger brother Saïd and hand his struggling side a 1-1 draw at Union Berlin on Sunday. It was the Billygoats' first away point of the league season. Cologne had thumped Union 5-0 at home in the German Cup second round only on Tuesday. The El Mala pair shared a pitch for Cologne's senior team for the first time on Sunday as 21-year-old Malek fired into the roof of the net on 79 minutes. His 20-year-old brother's cross had somehow found its way to him across the packed Union box. "I don't know what to say, it feels unbelievable," Malek told streaming portal DAZN. "It was a very important for us to get a point. We have really fought and expended lots of energy. But it's all indescribable." Germany winger Saïd had earlier missed Cologne's best chance up to that point when he shot over, moments after Malek had been introduced from the bench. The older but less experienced brother showed his sibling how it was done having only been on the field for seven minutes. Saïd added: "I'm happy for the lad, I see how hard he works. He has totally deserved it." Union had seized an early lead when Janik Haberer scored his second goal in two games having gone two seasons without netting in the league. The midfielder-turned-wingback prodded home after good work by Tim Skarke. The capital club are in the relegation play-off spot with seven points from eight games, while Cologne lie 13th on nine. Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hamburg 3-1 at home in Sunday's late game to leapfrog their 15th-placed opponents and power up to eighth in the tight standings. Younes Ebnoutalib and Raphael Onyedika struck in the second half to secure the win. Warmed Omari had netted an unlucky own goal on 10 minutes to boost Frankfurt, but Terem Moffi quickly spared his team-mate's blushes with an equalizer. Frankfurt brought Niko Iličević, the nephew of former Croatia international Ivo Iličević, off the bench for his debut just a day after his 16th birthday. On Saturday, Borussia Dortmund drew 2-2 at Bayern Munich to stay level on points with the leaders at the top of the Bundesliga.

item.title: Havertz becomes EPL's top German scorer in Arsenal win at Liverpool
item.description: Arsenal's Kai Havertz (2nd R) scores his side's first goal during the English Premier League soccer match between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield. (is associated with: «Havertz becomes EPL's top German scorer in Arsenal win at Liverpool») Peter Byrne/PA Wire/dpa Kai Havertz’s winning goal in Arsenal’s 1-0 triumph at Liverpool on Sunday made him the record German goalscorer in the Premier League. The Gunners forward surpassed the mark of former Manchester City midfielder İlkay Gündoğan when he tapped home his 46th goal in the competition after 16 minutes at Anfield. It was his third league strike of the campaign, taking his overall total for the north London club to 27, and sent the champions top of the table after City lost to Brighton on Saturday. Havertz scored 19 Premier League goals during his spell with Chelsea from 2020 to 2023, a period during which he also netted a Champions League final winner. Brighton’s Pascal Gross is the competition’s third most prolific German with 34, ahead of former Arsenal player Mesut Özil with 33. Other notable Germans on the list include former Tottenham favourite Jürgen Klinsmann with 29 and Michael Ballack, a Chelsea title-winner, with 17. Havertz’s Germany international team-mate Florian Wirtz, who hit the bar for Liverpool, has five goals to his name for the Reds.

item.title: Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten, OG Ezra Cleveland injured, able to return
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars suffered a key injury on the offensive line in the first quarter of their game on Nov. 1 against the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium. Starting right guard Ezra Cleveland limped off the field on the Jaguars ' second possession of the game following a 3-yard gain on a running back by Chris Rodriguez . Cleveland was able to get off the field under his own power but was taken into the blue medical tent and was seen in the second quarter sitting on the bench. He was replaced for the time being by second-year guard Wyatt Milum but was able to return. Cleveland was moved from left guard to right guard this season through a combination of a back injury to 2025 starter Patrick Mekari that has yet to heal, and the emergence of third-round rookie Emmanuel Pregnon . The Jaguars have already lost left tackle Anton Harrison to a season-ending knee injury. He has been replaced by Walker Little . Running back Bhayshul Tuten also came out briefly with an injury but missed only one offensive series. He gained 28 yards on six carries on the Jaguars' opening TD reception. item.title: Lakers vs. Raptors: Three things to watch as L.A. looks to bounce back
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers PG Luka Doncic (77) and G Austin Reaves (15) share a laugh before an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Thursday October 8, 2026 in Los Angeles, Calif. The Lakers showed how quickly their offense can build a lead Friday. They also showed how quickly that advantage can disappear. After surrendering a 25-point lead in a 112-95 loss to the Warriors, the Lakers (4-2) return to Crypto.com Arena to face the Toronto Raptors (3-2) on Sunday. Their seventh game presents another opportunity to address the uneven execution that has contributed to two losses in the last three games. Here are three things to watch. Can the Lakers take better care of the ball? The Lakers committed 20 turnovers against Golden State, with Austin Reaves responsible for eight. Luka Dončić’s 37 points helped fuel their offense, but L.A. struggled to sustain possessions as the Warriors recovered from their early deficit. Toronto presents another challenge for the Lakers’ ballhandlers. The Raptors are averaging 12.4 steals, which ranks second in the NBA through five games. The Lakers have already demonstrated their scoring ability. Turning more possessions into shot attempts would give that offense a better chance to hold up across four quarters. Will the reserves provide a response? Golden State’s bench outscored the Lakers’ reserves 50-7 on Friday, a significant disparity in a game L.A. lost by 17. That followed a win over the Clippers in which the Lakers received important contributions throughout the rotation without Dončić. Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton have shown they can bring scoring and defensive activity, but the Lakers need those contributions alongside their leading scorer, too, and at a consistent level. Watch how JJ Redick distributes the ballhandling responsibilities when he begins making substitutions. How will L.A. defend Scottie Barnes? Barnes enters Sunday after scoring a career-high 41 points in Toronto’s 121-114 loss to Orlando. He has led the Raptors in scoring in four of their first five games. His size and ability to operate inside present a different defensive assignment from chasing Golden State’s shooters. The Lakers must make Barnes work for positioning while keeping their help organized behind the initial defender. Allowing him to establish himself deep in the paint would put additional pressure on Walker Kessler to protect the rim. How L.A. handles those possessions without surrendering open looks elsewhere will be central to its response. After losing control of Friday’s game, the Lakers need a more connected defensive effort to finish their first meeting with Toronto.

item.title: Lazio pull clear at Serie A summit as Gattuso warns of vertigo
item.description: Lazio forward Andrea Pinamonti celebrates after scoring his team's second goal (tiziana fabi) Gennaro Gattuso's Lazio consolidated their position at the top of Serie A on Sunday with a 2-1 victory over Cagliari, nudging ahead of Inter Milan after the two clubs had started the weekend level on points. Lazio made a poor start as Cagliari took the lead through M'Bala Nzola in the 20th minute before goals in either half from Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti gave them a sixth straight Serie A win. With 28 points from 10 games, Lazio moved three clear of Inter after they lost the Milan derby. Unbeaten Roma sit third on 24 points and Como climbed back to fourth with a 1-0 win over rock-bottom Venezia. Lazio last won Serie A in 2000 and this is the best start to a league campaign in the club's history but the Roman outfit's ambitions remain modest according to Gattuso. "Our target is to avoid relegation and we still need 12 more points," Gattuso said. "We need to get our heads down and work, and not look at the table." Some Lazio fans aren't watching at all. As has been the case in recent home matches, Lazio played in front of largely empty sections of the Stadio Olimpico, with many ultras and supporters continuing their boycott in protest against owner and president Claudio Lotito, whom they accuse of failing to invest sufficiently in the squad. Como's victory at home over lowly Venezia on Sunday was a fifth consecutive victory across all competitions. The hosts dominated, but needed a penalty to find the back of the net. Como captain Lucas Da Cunha converted in the 43rd minute for the French international's first goal of the season. "This is the type of match we found hard to win last season," Da Cunha told DAZN. Cesc Fabregas's side had slipped to fifth when AC Milan beat champions Inter 3-1 on Saturday. Como moved one point behind Roma, who beat Udinese 5-2 on Saturday. "This victory is really important in terms of our maturing process," said Fabregas. "Our state of mind is irreproachable," added the 39-year-old Spaniard. Como resume their Champions League campaign against Lens on Wednesday. In a season in which Italian teams have struggled in Europe, Como have the best record of the Serie A clubs in the Champions League, sitting ninth in the 36-team standings, with six points from three games. Como, who were playing in Italy's third division as recently as 2021, beat Manchester United 4-1 in the last round of European matches. jr/dmc/mw

item.title: From Barcelona’s captain to Anfield’s cult hero: The blooming Ronald Araujo-Liverpool love affair
item.description: From Barcelona’s captain to Anfield’s cult hero: The blooming Ronald Araujo-Liverpool love affair There is something wonderful about watching Ronald Araujo celebrate a goal at Anfield. On October 20, Liverpool were trailing Villarreal 2-1. Having already been two goals down, Andoni Iraola’s men were desperate to get back on level terms before half-time. Minutes into first-half stoppage time, Rio Ngumoha picked up the ball and delivered a teasing cross towards the far post. The Reds youngster put a bit more on the ball than he should have, but Araujo refused to give up on it, arriving behind the defenders and heading home Liverpool’s equaliser . Then came the moment that told the bigger story. The former Barcelona defender’s momentum carried him into the Anfield Road stand, where he found himself among jubilant Liverpool supporters. For a few seconds at Anfield that night, the boundaries between a footballer and a fan disappeared. Arms reached towards him. Strangers embraced him. Liverpool eventually won the game 4-3, but the celebration felt more exhilarating than any of the seven goals scored on Merseyside that night. Araujo has been an unexpected hit at Liverpool.(Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images) For Barcelona supporters, watching it all u nfold stirred rather complicated emotions. A defender who struggled to convince towards the end of his time in Catalonia is becoming one of the most loved players among Liverpool supporters. Anfield is falling in love with the Araujo Barcelona once knew Football supporters often recognise passion before they notice technical ability. Sometimes, all it takes to win over a crowd is someone willing to put his body somewhere others would hesitate to put a foot. Against Brighton & Hove Albion last weekend, Araujo provided the perfect example of this. Having already gone to ground, he somehow managed to push the ball away from Maxim de Cuyper’s path with his head. Later in the game, a thunderous, full-blooded, clean challenge on Malick Yalcouye brought another enormous roar from the Anfield crowd. They celebrated these Araujo interventions like goals. His performance in the 2-0 victory over the Seagulls earned him the Premier League Player of the Matchweek award. Araujo registered eight clearances and won every ground and aerial duel he contested. Jamie Carragher, a Reds legend, had already called Araujo a cult hero back in September, just weeks into his Liverpool career. Yet the most interesting part of this growing affection is how it feels like déjà vu . Barcelona supporters remember this version of Araujo. The defender who threw himself into challenges, chased down seemingly unstoppable attackers and made defending look like an art. Those qualities once made him indispensable at the Spotify Camp Nou . Now, 1,000 miles away, they are once again making him indispensable to another fanbase. The complicated ending to Araujo’s Barcelona story It is easy to forget how quickly Araujo’s fortunes changed at Barcelona

item.title: Tributes to 'inspirational' Olympian Ciara Mageean after death at 34
item.description: A statement posted on Mageean's social media on Sunday said she died surrounded by her loved ones [Getty Images] Tributes have been paid to former European champion and two-time Olympic runner Ciara Mageean, who has died at the age of 34. Mageean, from Portaferry in County Down, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025. She died on Sunday morning, surrounded by her loved ones, a statement posted on her social media accounts said. "A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed," it said. Mageean's death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to her long-term partner Thomas Moran . The athlete represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics and won gold in the 1500m at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in 2024. She also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning silver in Birmingham in 2022. 'One of our own' Olympic legend Lady Mary Peters said Mageean was a "wonderful lady" who was "gracious, beautiful, talented and inspirational to the next generation". "We knew she was very ill and we knew that it was inevitable but we didn't expect it so soon," said the 1972 Olympic pentathlon gold medallist. Lady Mary's charity the Mary Peters Trust, which supports Northern Ireland athletes, had helped Mageean in her athletics career. "My charity supported her for as long as we could because she was so talented and we recognised that in her," said Last Mary. She said that Mageean had continued to inspire young athletes even while undergoing treatment for cancer and would be "sorely missed in the world of sport". Mageean won a gold medal at the 2024 European Championships in Rome [Getty Images] Sean Young, the secretary of Portaferry Gaelic Athletic Club, where Mageean played camogie in her younger years, said its members were in "disbelief and shock" at her death. He said Mageean had been a "fierce competitor" who began her sporting journey at the club before pursuing athletics. "Outside the sporting arena she is the most inspirational, humble person we have ever had within our club," he said. Obituary: Gifted athlete whose wit and smile left lasting impression Two-time Olympian Mageean dies aged 34 Down Gaelic Athletic Association (GAA) said it was "honoured and privileged" to call Mageean one of its own, describing her as someone who never forgot her roots. "She touched the lives of so many people and she helped change the lives of so many," it said. "In her battle with illness she showed us courage, positivity and the value of life." Her former school, Assumption Grammar in Ballynahinch, County Down, said it was "deeply saddened and heartbroken" by the death of its "cherished past pupil". "Ciara's kindness, strength, faith and unwavering determination were an inspiration to us all," it said. "She touched countless lives with her warmth, humility and generosity of spirit." item.title: Jessie Bates’ forced touchback is one of NFL’s best defensive plays this year in Falcons-Bucs
item.description: Jessie Bates is widely considered one of the best safeties in the NFL. The Atlanta Falcons star is particularly good at forcing takeaways, and he just proved it again during one of the wildest plays of the season so far in his team’s Week 8 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Bucs QB Baker Mayfield fumbled the snap, picked up the ball, started to scramble, then lateraled it to running back Bucky Irving in what looked like a college football option play. Irving was making his way to an open end zone when Bates came in with his signature Peanut Punch to knock the ball free inside of the one-yard-line and out of the end zone for a touchdown. Talk about a game-breaking play. Watch Bates’ forced fumble here: WILD PLAY IN TAMPA. item.title: Pat Freiermuth Reaches Significant Steelers Milestone
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth during a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth has surpassed Bennie Cunningham (2,879) to become the Steelers’ second-leading tight end in career receiving yards. Only Steelers legend Heath Miller (6,569) has more receiving yards among tight ends in franchise history. Freiermuth moved into second place with a 7-yard reception late in the first quarter. Last year, Freiermuth recorded a career low in offensive snap percentage (51%), targets per game (3.2) and receiving yards per game (2.4), yet he had his most efficient season when it came to yards per target (9) and yards per catch (11). Things have changed now under Mike McCarthy . Freiermuth is off to a hot start, catching 24 passes for 2007 yards and four touchdowns. Freiermuth feels like he’s being properly utilized. “I definitely see myself as more of a focal point of the offense,” Freiermuth said in early October on The Pat McAfee Show . “Probably in OTAs and camp, I started getting the feel that Aaron [Rodgers] and Coach McCarthy were going to use me and my strengths. And I felt like it was just kind of a natural process, trying to lean on the tight end room with me and Darnell [Washington] throughout the camp and OTAs. Freiermuth had a standout performance in the Steelers ’ Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts, catching seven passes for 44 yards and two touchdowns. “I think Coach McCarthy has done a great job of challenging the offense to go out and win games on offense instead of kind of relying on the defense to win those games for us,” Freiermuth said. “I feel like we’re playing some good complementary team football right now and we just gotta continue to keep going.” Freiermuth also praised McCarthy for being very detailed. “I thought he was going to be extremely detailed, and he definitely is that,” Freiermuth said. “Our schedules are very detailed, very oriented. We’re in there throughout the day, really going through meetings throughout the whole day and very structured, which is good. item.title: How Oklahoma State football's widespread defensive faults cost Cowboys vs Iowa State
item.description: AMES, IA — Oklahoma State linebacker Ethan Wesloski’s answers were short. He didn't have much to say about his defense’s performance in a 51-49 loss at Iowa State. “I didn’t play good enough, didn’t play to the standard, simple,” Wesloski said. The 51 points OSU’s defense allowed Saturday are the most the Cowboys have allowed in a game this season. Those points sting worse because of the 49 points quarterback Drew Mestemaker and the offense scored. “It hurts, especially when you know Drew and them are rolling,” defensive end James Williams said. More: Oklahoma State football WR Wyatt Young apologizes for penalty vs Iowa State Seven touchdowns, a seventh-consecutive 300-yard passing game from Mestemaker, 275 total yards from running back Caleb Hawkins and a go-ahead touchdown pitch to receiver Wyatt Young with 53 seconds remaining couldn’t overcome OSU’s defensive problems. Saturday’s scene in Ames isn’t new. Williams said it felt just like the Colorado game, where seemingly every Cowboy touchdown was answered by the defense giving up a score. For the fifth consecutive game, OSU trailed at halftime. Just like in a 35-32 loss to Houston, it felt like whichever defense was on the field last would be the loser and OSU's defense couldn’t get rid of the hot potato. With 53 seconds left, Iowa State quarterback Jaylen Raynor connected on a 33-yard pass down the sideline to freshman receiver Jamal Polite Jr. to get Cyclones into field goal territory. It was the seventh Iowa State play that went for 25 or more yards. Cyclone running back Aiden Flora ran for runs of 4, 3 and 7 yards on his way to a 221-yard day to set up kicker Kyle Konrardy’s walk-off 34-yard field goal. Failures on multiple levels led to OSU allowing 581 yards to Iowa State. That’s the most yardage Iowa State’s offense has tallied in a Big 12 game since 2016, when the Cyclones went for 608 against Texas. Just last week, the Cyclones scored three points against Arizona and finished with 221 total yards. That game, a tight end led Iowa State with 42 receiving yards and Raynor was benched at halftime. There were factors against OSU’s defense. The team’s leading tackler, linebacker Tate Romney, exited in the third quarter with a hamstring injury. Defensive end Jaleel Johnson appeared on the sideline in the second half with his arm in a sling. The slick grass in Jack Trice Stadium favored both offenses. because ballcarriers knew where they were going. Ask around the locker room, and those challenges aren’t the reason OSU’s defense struggled so much Saturday. item.title: Bulls’ Rebuild Hides A Surprising Rebound Edge
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images The Chicago Bulls are losing games at a historic pace, yet they are crashing the offensive glass better than most other teams in the league. This 29.2% team offensive rebound rate ranks 10th among all 30 NBA franchises, according to Basketball Reference data cited by Pippen Ain’t Easy . For a team with a dismal 1-5 mark across the opening six contests of the 2026-27 season, this statistic is peculiar. Chicago faces Philadelphia on Monday night at 7:30 p.m. EST in a matchup that highlights the gap between the two squads. The 76ers sit first in the Eastern Conference with a 6-1 record, while the Bulls trail in 13th place at 1-5, per FOX Sports . Philadelphia finished the previous season with a 23-18 home record. and averaged 32.4 bench points, showing depth the Bulls simply do not have right now. The Bulls shot 46.9% from the field last season, but their current form suggests they are far from that level of efficiency. The Cost of a Total Tear-Down The front office made bold moves during the 2026 NBA Trade Deadline that stripped the roster of its veteran core. Guards Coby White and Ayo Dosunmu were traded away, along with starting center Nikola Vucevic, according to Pippen Ain’t Easy. The team made extensive changes intended to reset the franchise for the future. The new leadership under Bryson Graham continued this momentum by trading guard Rob Dillingham for Buddy Hield in the late 2026 offseason. Some might argue this approach is too risky, but the data shows the team is bottom-ranked in both offensive and defensive efficiency. The Bulls sit 26th in offense and 28th in defense across the entire NBA, per Pippen Ain’t Easy. Such a trajectory rivals the losing basketball of the Tim Floyd era, a painful reminder for supporters recalling those grim periods. Who Can Stop the Bleeding? Monday night brings a tough test against a Philadelphia squad that is injury‑hit and hungry. The 76ers have key players like LeBron James and Joel Embiid listed as out, but they still possess a roster built to win now, according to FOX Sports. The Bulls will need to avoid the self-inflicted wounds that cost them against Boston earlier in the week. Chicago turned the ball over 24 times in the loss, giving their opponent 39 points off turnovers, per Sports Illustrated. Fixing those errors is the only way to stop the four-game skid. Dailyn Swain is day to day with a back issue, while Nic Claxton is out with a hamstring strain for the Bulls, per FOX Sports.
